title: a --confirm that does not match the content is refused, whether it was never right or the draft changed after the owner read it; nothing is saved
source: intended: docs/decisions.md D7 and B3-18/B3-19 (a draft becomes a build only with the owner's OK: a terminal, or the token of the content he read; the guard denies the agent)
intent: INTENDED behavior (defect N-15, drafts; docs/decisions.md D7). `--confirm <x>` must equal the first 12 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the bytes that would be written, so it binds the OK to the content that was read. A token that never matched, a malformed one, and a token of a draft that was edited afterwards are all `JITSO REJECTED: --confirm <x> does not match the draft (it changed, or the token is wrong); nothing saved`, exit 2: the file is shown first, nothing is written and the draft is kept. The oracle has no `build save` (the runner maps only `build list`): it answers `unknown command` on stderr with exit 2 and prints nothing on stdout, so every expectation that needs the `+ ` lines, the token text or the written file FAILS on it.
